Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Class Desktop2DCompositorHost

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.Desktop2DCompositorHost
public final class Desktop2DCompositorHost extends Object
Hosts composited native X11 windows inside the conventional 2D desktop: when lg3d runs as the X11 window manager + compositor, each redirected client window is given a Desktop2DWindow whose content is the Swing surface painted by a CompositedWindowHost, so a real external application (a browser, a terminal, ...) appears as an ordinary MDI window in the 2D desktop rather than escaping as a separate top-level window owned by the host window manager.

This controller is the desktop-side bookkeeping only — it owns the windowId -> Desktop2DWindow map and forwards the compositor's map/resize/retitle/unmap notifications. It reaches the X server exclusively through the CompositedWindowHost seam, which keeps this package free of Java 3D and of gnu.x11, so the whole map/dispatch lifecycle is unit-testable headlessly with a fake host and a fake opener.

All methods are expected to run on the EDT (the compositor's window-manager notifications are marshalled here by the desktop).

    • windowMapped

      public void windowMapped(int windowId, String title, int width, int height)
      Handles a client window becoming viewable: opens a hosted surface and a desktop window for it. A re-map of an already-hosted window is folded into a resize + retitle rather than a duplicate.
      Parameters:
      windowId - the X window id
      title - the window title
      width - the window width in pixels
      height - the window height in pixels

    • windowResized

      public void windowResized(int windowId, int width, int height)
      Handles a client window resize. No-op for a window that is not hosted.
      Parameters:
      windowId - the X window id
      width - the new width in pixels
      height - the new height in pixels

    • windowRetitled

      public void windowRetitled(int windowId, String title)

      windowId - the X window id
      title - the new title
